t: Alfonso VIII marched to Alarcos without waiting for the reinforcements coming from Alfonso IX of León and Sancho VII of Navarre.
The Castilian heavy cavalry broke the Almohad front lines and killed the vizier, but the Arab left enveloped its flank and rear and al-Mansur's rearguard then attacked.
The victory proved short-lived: al-Mansur went back to Africa in 1198, and his successor Muhammad al-Nasir was defeated at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212.
dyk: Pedro Fernández de Castro, who held a personal feud against Alfonso, rode with the Almohads and was sent by the caliph to negotiate the surrender of the castle of Alarcos.
ev: Al-Mansur recaptures Silves from Portugal and returns to his capital, and an armistice with the Christian kings follows
At the end of the truce Alfonso invades southern al-Andalus, led by the Archbishop of Toledo and the Order of Calatrava
Al-Mansur lands at Tarifa on 1 June and reaches Córdoba on 30 June
The Almohad army crosses the Muradal pass and destroys a Christian cavalry detachment, while Alfonso marches from Toledo to Alarcos
On Wednesday 18 July the Almohads defeat the Castilian army at Alarcos, and Alfonso flees to Toledo
Many nearby castles, among them Calatrava and Malagón, surrender or are abandoned, and al-Mansur takes the title al-Mansur Billah
Al-Mansur returns to Africa, and he dies in February 1199
Al-Mansur's successor Muhammad al-Nasir is defeated at Las Navas de Tolosa

f.place: Alarcos (al-Arak in Arabic), near the Guadiana River, the southern limit of the Kingdom of Castile, in what is now central Spain; the Almohad army formed around a small hill called La Cabeza, two bow-shots from Alarcos
f.sides: The Almohads under the caliph Abu Yusuf Ya'qub al-Mansur, with his vizier Abu Yahya ibn Abi Hafs commanding the vanguard; Castile under King Alfonso VIII, whose heavy cavalry, about 8,000 strong, was led by Diego López de Haro
f.outcome: The Almohads won; the Castilian field army was destroyed and Alfonso fled to Toledo. The garrison of the unfinished fortress of Alarcos surrendered on terms and many nearby castles fell or were abandoned.
